limits.handling: Four egg-string portions treated as sibling cohorts without reported genomic parentage verification. Approximately 30 cm/100–150 eggs is collected portion description, not complete female clutch range. Stage 22 transfer, two-week rearing at 18 C and stage 30–35 tests are laboratory context, not natural growth/thermal limits.

90 subjects tested once each. Ten unfamiliar sibling versus ten nonsibling stimuli; repeated observation seconds and 60 minutes per subject are not independent subjects. Individual zone-time proportions analysed; clutch included as fixed factor. Equal stimulus groups do not test group-size preference.

No significant side preference in four treatments does not prove no kin-recognition ability, exact equality or absence across populations and later life stages. Odour/genetic cue differences and adult learned recognition remain proposed.

Isolation neutral-zone term t=3.155, p=0.002 retained. Individual stimulus-side social terms nonsignificant. General locomotor activity not independently measured; social responsiveness versus general movement cannot be separated. No stress hormones or neural circuitry measured.

Tap/pond rearing and test water matched, not independently crossed. Nonsignificant water terms do not establish equivalence of all natural waters or isolate developmental versus immediate cues. No microbial or chemical mechanism measured.

Predator avoidance, warning-colour functions, group-size importance and neural changes are partly other-taxon background/hypotheses, not direct experiments here. Adult behaviour, persistence after metamorphosis, mating, fitness, current distribution and conservation status unmeasured.
